units.source_text: 看罢画册，两人相与谈话，直到天色近晓之时方才就寝。

en.t: After they had finished looking through the picture album, the two of them talked together and did not go to bed until dawn was nearly breaking.

units.source_text: 二女公子叫浮舟睡在她身旁，和她谈父亲生前之事，以及多年来蛰居宇治山庄时情状，

en.t: The Second Princess had Ukifune sleep beside her and spoke with her about their father while he was alive, and about the circumstances of her many years living secluded at the Uji villa,

units.source_text: 虽不从头至尾，却也漫谈了不少。

en.t: though she did not tell everything from beginning to end, she still talked at length about many things.

units.source_text: 浮舟非常想念亡父，可惜终于不得和他见面，不胜悲伤。

en.t: Ukifune deeply missed her late father, and grieving that in the end she had never been able to meet him, she was overcome with sorrow.

units.source_text: 知道昨夜之事的侍女中有一人说：“实际情况不知究竟怎样？

en.t: One of the waiting women who knew about the events of the previous night said, "I wonder what really happened after all?

units.source_text: 这位美貌的小姐，夫人虽然异常怜爱，然而已被玷污，怜爱也徒然了，真可怜啊！”

en.t: This beautiful young lady is cherished so very much by her mother, but if she has already been defiled, all that affection is in vain. How pitiful she is!"

units.source_text: 右近答道：“不，没有这回事。

en.t: Ukon answered, "No, nothing of the kind happened.

units.source_text: 那乳母拉住了我，向我仔细诉说，听她说来确无此事。

en.t: That nurse stopped me and told me the whole story in detail, and from what she said, there truly was no such incident.

units.source_text: 亲王出门时，口中也吟唱着‘相逢犹似不相逢’的古歌。

en.t: When the prince left, he was also murmuring the old poem, 'Meeting is still like not meeting.'

units.source_text: 但也难说，也许是故意吟唱此歌的吧？

en.t: But it is hard to say; perhaps he recited that poem on purpose?
What really happened cannot be known.

units.source_text: 不过昨夜灯光中细看这位小姐的神情，非常安详，不像是有过什么事情的。”

en.t: Still, when I looked closely at the young lady's expression in the lamplight last night, she was very calm, and did not seem as though anything had happened."

units.source_text: 她们悄悄地议论此事，都可怜这浮舟。

en.t: They discussed the matter quietly among themselves, and all of them pitied Ukifune.
